title: Queued deadline relaxation + starvation breaker for continuous-batcher scheduler
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Improves tail latency and prevents queue starvation under KV-heavy and heterogeneous kernel workloads. No API changes. Config knobs for scheduler tuning added.
body: Context and motivation: Continuous batching delivers high throughput for short LLM requests but can suffer from starvation and tail latency regressions when a small fraction of requests require slow kernels, heavyweight KV prefetches, or large sequence lengths. We observed recurring incidents where long-running requests held batch slots and caused head-of-queue starvation for latency-sensitive traffic (see linked playbook SUP-1182). This PR introduces a soft-deadline relaxation + starvation-breaker mechanism in the continuous-batcher scheduler to allow fair forward progress without sacrificing batching efficiency. -- What this PR does (summary): 1) Adds per-request soft_deadline and queued_deadline_relaxation policies: requests get a soft deadline derived from their SLO class + historical kernel latency distribution. If a queued request's soft deadline is breached, the scheduler is allowed to relax coalescing of that request into large batches (favoring smaller, earlier dispatch) or opportunistically schedule a hedged duplicate on an alternate slot. 2) Introduces a starvation_breaker token that periodically preemptively reserves a small fraction of batch capacity for long-waiting small requests to ensure progress under skewed workloads. The token is credit-based and decays to avoid harming throughput. 3) Integrates KV-cache hints into admission decisions: requests that touch recently-prefetched KV keys get preferential placement to avoid repeated expensive fetches, while requests likely to cause expensive cache churn are limited to conservatively-sized batches. 4) Adds kernel-aware pacing: the scheduler uses per-kernel estimate percentiles (P50/P95) to steer batch formation and avoid packing many P95-heavy requests together. 5) Exposes runtime tunables (max_relaxation_ms, starvation_token_fraction, kernel_p95_threshold) and adds telemetry for wait_time_by_slo, starvation_breaker_fires, and relaxed_dispatch_count. -- Why this approach: Full preemption of in-flight batched work is expensive and risks GPU kernel fragmentation. Instead, soft-deadline relaxation and small hedges keep the fast-path intact while ensuring that latency-sensitive requests see bounded waits. The starvation breaker provides a lightweight admission control that trades a tiny amount of throughput headroom for substantially better fairness. Kernel-aware batching reduces the probability of microbursts of slow work landing in the same dispatch. -- Implementation highlights: - scheduler/continuous/queued_scheduler.go: core algorithm changes (deadline computation, relaxation heuristics, token circuit). - scheduler/continuous/kv_admission.go: KV hint integration and eviction-avoid logic. - runtime/kernels/estimator.go: small per-kernel percentile estimator (exponentially-weighted) used by the scheduler. - telemetry/metrics_registry.go: new metrics and dashboard configs. - tests/scheduler/queued_relaxation_test.go: unit tests for deadline relaxation and starvation breaker behavior. - perf/bench/relaxation_bench.py: microbench harness used for benchmarks in the PR. -- Commits (high-level): [1] compute per-request soft_deadline and plumbing into admission path; [2] implement queued_deadline_relaxation and token logic; [3] add kv hint integration and conservative batch sizing heuristics; [4] kernel percentile estimator and pacing logic; [5] metrics, dashboard wiring and docs; [6] tests and perf harness; [7] address reviewer feedback and tune defaults. -- Files changed (high level): - scheduler/continuous/queued_scheduler.go (+210/-48) - scheduler/continuous/kv_admission.go (+86/-12) - runtime/kernels/estimator.go (+42/-6) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (+30/-4) - tests/scheduler/queued_relaxation_test.go (+150/-0) - perf/bench/relaxation_bench.py (+22/-0) - docs/ops/scheduler-tuning.md (+80/-58) -- Benchmarks and results: Microbench runs on a 4xA100 (simulated multi-tenant mix) with a skewed mix: 85% short chat (<=128 tokens), 10% medium (<=512), 5% long (>=1024) where the long requests map to P95 kernels that are ~6x slower than P50. Baselines (main, before changes): P95 end-to-end latency for short class = 265ms. With queued_deadline_relaxation + starvation breaker: P95 short class = 160ms (-40%), P99 = 270ms (-28%). Overall throughput unchanged within 1-2% during steady-state. KV-heavy synthetic workload: tail latency reduced by 35% and cache churn decreased (measured by kv_eviction_rate metric). -- Backwards compatibility and rollout: Defaults are conservative (max_relaxation_ms=50ms, starvation_token_fraction=0.03). All knobs are runtime-configurable via operator flags and can be toggled per-cluster. No API surface changes. Rollout plan: feature gate off by default for private deployments; enable behind an experiment flag for Dedicated/Hosted gradually (Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) while monitoring new metrics. -- Tests and CI: Unit tests cover correctness of deadline math, starvation token decay, and hedged dispatch scenarios. Integration perf bench reproduces benchmark numbers. CI initially reported a flaky kernel-scheduling test; rerun passed. -- Review conversation (short): David: suggested exposing kernel_p95_threshold and lowering default relaxation; Marco: requested end-to-end bench numbers and suggested moving kv hint thresholds into admission.algo; Rina: asked for dashboard widgets and alert thresholds. Addressed feedback by adding extra metrics and moving thresholds into admission config. Final approvals: all reviewers approved. -- Risk and mitigations: Risk that hedging increases duplicate work slightly (measured <0.6% extra tokens in bench). Mitigation: hedges disabled by default and only fire when soft_deadline breached. Starvation token is small fraction to keep throughput intact. -- Merge and follow-ups: Squash-merged to main. Follow-ups: ENG-2152 (auto-tune kernel_p95_threshold from telemetry), ENG-2160 (operator UI to tune starvation token).
